AGREEMENT
ARTICLE I
RECOGNITION AND JURISDICTION

A. The Employer recognizes IF&CWU Local No. 408 as the exclusive and collective bargaining agent for all employees working in the Meat Department at all of Employer's retail stores located in the following counties: Arenas, Austin, Bastrop, Bell, Brazos, Galveston, Grimes, Hardin, Harris, Jasper, Jackson, Jefferson, Polk, Liberty, Walker, Lee, Liberty, Matagorda, Milam, Montgomery, Nacogdoches, Orange, Panola, Polk, Refugio, San Jacinto, San Patricio, Jefferson, Winn, Tyler, Victoria, Walker, Walker, Wharton, Washington, and Wharton. The parties agree that this Contract shall cover, the Union which is a party hereto, shall have jurisdiction over all Meat Department employees of the Employer who are, or will be, owned or leased, operated by the Employer in such counties.

It is hereby agreed that the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall be binding upon the successors and/or assigns of the Employer. In the event of a change in ownership of the operation, the Company shall pay off all obligations under this Agreement to the Union and the employees.  The Company shall pay monetary benefits due employees under the terms of this Agreement at the time of transfer of ownership.

B. For the purpose of this Contract, the Meat Department includes all employees who are engaged in the handling, processing, and offering for sale of fresh meat, poultry, processed poultry, fish, rabbits, sausages, smoked meats and meat products, which has customarily been performed by bargaining unit employees in the stores continuing within the jurisdiction of the Union, regardless of the bargaining unit's current composition, (1) to the extent such functions continue to be performed by the Employer, (2) to the extent such work is performed by the Employer, (3) in the Union's geographical area of representation as set forth above, and (3) to the extent such work is not currently represented by another Union. Specifically, although some duties previously performed by bargaining unit employees in designated geographical areas are covered by this Agreement, the Employer will continue to recognize the Union and work's collective bargaining jurisdiction over the Employer's store delicatessen operations that existed prior to the execution of this Agreement. If the Employer decides to open a delicatessen in any of the counties in the markets may continue to do so to the extent this service are presently performed.

C. It is not intended by any provision of this Agreement to prevent the Employer from cutting, packaging or otherwise handling meat dining at any central point. The Employer agrees that any work of cutting, packaging or otherwise handling meat at any central point owned, leased, or operated by the Employer in the counties listed in Paragraph A above which was previously performed by bargaining unit employees shall remain the work of the employees of this bargaining unit under the wages, hours and working conditions of this Contract, except where this work is under the jurisdiction of an existing collective bargaining contract with the Employer. New classifications may be established as necessary. The Employer agrees that the establishment of new positions shall not prematurely embrace work being performed by employees in any established classification. Prior to establishing such a new classification, the Employer and the Union shall confer to establish the wage rate for such classification. In the event the parties cannot agree after such conference, the Employer may establish such a new classification and rate.

ARTICLE II
NON-DISCRIMINATION—CHECK-OFF

A. There shall be no discrimination against any employee, whether by the Employer or the Union, because of their membership or nonmembership in the Union.

B. The Employer and the Union agree that neither shall discriminate against any employee because of age, race, creed, color, sex or national origin. It is understood that wherever there appears a reference in this collective bargaining agreement to male or female gender, the intent is to interpret such reference as applying to both males and females.

C. The Employer shall, during the term of this Contract, deduct finition fees and regular union dues weekly from employees who are members of the Union and who individually and voluntarily certify in writing authorization for such deductions. The Employer shall remit all sums deducted in this manner to the Union.

A uniform Active Labor Ball dutuction will be made in January of each year for those employees who indicate, in writing, year authorization to do so, and forwarded will be to the Local Union.

D. It is agreed that the Company will not attempt in any manner to prevent or discourage any employee from joining the Union or engaging in any lawful activity associated therewith. The Company agrees to tell new employees that they are operating under a Union contract.

E. Employers with facilities and capabilities, which have no employee credit union, agree to make weekly deductions in amounts designated by employees belonging to the UFCW Local Union No. 408 Federal Credit Union who desire to see such deductions and shall remit these amounts to such credit union.

ARTICLE III
NO STRIKE—NO LOCKOUT

A. The Union agrees not to cause, ratify or sanction any strike, slowdown, or stoppage of work and the Employer agrees that there shall be no lockout of any employees during the term of this Contract.

B. The Employer agrees that nothing in this Contract shall require any employee to report or perform to any work when do so will require her to access a legal prob job picket line in a primary labor dispute involving the Employer wherein the Union has sanctioned such a picket.  In order to be eligible, however, that UFCW Local No. 408 agrees that it will give the Employer at least forty-eight (48) hours notice after such primary picket simmering commences of its intention to sanction any such primary picket picket line.

ARTICLE IV
MEAT DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES

A. Each shop shall have a Head meat Cutter and he shall be a Journeyman Meat Cutter and he may perform the duties of the Cut off, and shall direct the work, movements and operations of the Meat Department employees.

B. A Journeyman is one who has qualified as a skilled Meat Cutter. His duties shall include the receiving, cutting, grinding, slicing, skinning, preparing, processing, sealing, wrapping, bagging, pricing, fabricating and serving of all items in the Meat Department and the performance of all the work indicated art term of this Agreement.

C. Any Apprentice must be eighteen (18) years of age or older, learning all details and developing skills for performing the duties of a Journeyman Meat Cutter. The Employer agrees to assign each Apprentice to various jobs in order that he may learn all the duties of a Journeyman Meat Cutter. The apprenticeship training period shall be for a two-year period.

In cases where the Apprentice has not qualified as a Journeyman at the end of the apprenticeship training period in the judgment of the Employer, the apprenticeship training period may be extended an additional six (6) months and the Apprentice shall be paid the Apprentice rate during the extension period.

Nothing in this Section C will prevent the Employer from advancing an Apprentice to a Journeyman before the end of the apprenticeship training period if, in the judgment of the Employer, the Apprentice is qualified.

D. Employees engaged in weighing, wrapping and pricing and displaying shall be qualified as Wrappers. In other words, Wrappers may be employed to weigh, scale, price, label, bag, display, box, tray, wrap, etc. Wrappers may be employed to stock meats and slice cheeses, bacon, boxed treats, tray meats and delicatessen items with slicing machines, and to clean work tables and any equipment that they work with, including removers, scrapers, etc. Wrappers may be employed to clean the meat department and refrigerated conveyor troughs, but excluding cleaning electric sawing wires, grinders, tenderizers and poultry chopping machines. Wrappers shall not be permitted to cut any red meat, pork, lamb, poultry, rabbits, or fish.

Employees in the Weighers and Wrappers classification will have the opportunity to advance to the Journeyman seniority or reduction in straight-time hourly wage rate to the Apprentice classification, when a vacancy exists in Apprentice, provided they have the skills, abilities and physical capacity to perform the work. Employees in the Weighers and Wrappers classification may make a written request for such advancement, and shall do so in writing with copies to both the Employer's designated official and the Union.

When a Wrapper is assigned to the Journeyman or Apprentice classification for a period of probation, the Wrapper shall remain in the Wrapper classification for a period of ninety (90) days. If the Employer determines that the Wrapper continues to be assigned to the Apprentice or Journeyman classification, as his or her seniority date will be the date he was assigned as an Apprentice or Journeyman. If the former Wrapper is to be laid off, the former Wrapper may return to the Wrapper classification, and his or her seniority date shall be the date he was laid off. If the former Wrapper elects this option, his or her seniority date shall be the date he was originally assigned as a Wrapper.

If the former Wrapper has returned to the Wrapper classification and is recalled to the Journeyman or Apprentice classification, the Wrapper may accept the recall to the Journeyman or Apprentice classification, the Wrapper may accept the recall to the Journeyman or Apprentice classification without further recourse right to the Journeyman or Apprentice salaries.

A Wrapper with one (1) year of full-time zat service with the Employer shall receive six (6) months credit upon entrance to apprentice training.

E. Employees of the Seafood Department shall perform work in that department and shall be considered as part of the bargaining unit Part of Meat Department sales. The senior Seafood Clerk by store shall have the right to start the first forty (40) hour schedule available in their department.

F. The Employer and the Union agree that any qualified employee eighten (10) years of age, regardless of race, creed, color, sex, or national nationality shall be given an equal opportunity to work in any job classification covered by this Contract.

G. Head Meat Cutters shall be allowed to voluntarily return to the Journeyman classification without loss of seniority upon the giving of thirty (30) days written notice to the Company. The seniority of the Head Meat Cutter for the period he has been a Head Meat Cutter shall be conditioned upon the Employer having a qualified Head Meat Cutter replacement readily available to assume the responsibilities of the Head Meat Cutter during return to the Journeyman classification.

ARTICLE V
WAGES

A. The scale of wages and job classifications in Appendix A is attached hereto and made a part of this Contract.

B. Employer agrees to continue the past practice of giving credit for previous employment proven comparable experience in the retail food industry to any full-time employee. Such previous experience shall be considered to be must be considered within three (3) years and immediately prior to date of hire, excluding Military Service, and must be provably performed specifically on application for employment. Proof of previous comparable experience must be furnished by the employee or former employer. Such proof must be furnished within thirty (30) days after hire, in order to have such experience considered. Any rate increase shall not take effect until the experience has been verified and will become effective as of the date of verification.

C. Newly employed employees shall be classified by the Union as to their qualifications for Journeymen and Apprentices.

D. When a Journeyman Meat Cutter is designated by the Employer to relieve the Head Meat Cutter for a period of more than two (2) consecutive scheduled working days, said Journeyman shall receive the rate specified in this Contract for the Head Meat Cutter for the period of time actually worked. But, after two scheduled weekly days off of the Head Meat Cutter will not be utilized to compute the time worked in that classification by any Journeyman.

ARTICLE VI
HOURS OF WORK

A. Forty (40) hours of work, to be worked in five (5) days shall constitute a full workweek. Full-time employees who are scheduled for forty (40) hours in one given week shall be guaranteed forty (40) hours, in pay or len you leave that, for his or her seniority, the employee is not laid off. If the employee is not laid off, the employee is tarde, absentee, or has been disciplined just for cause. It is further understood that this guarantee will not apply when time off is granted by mutual agreement between the Employer and the employee or in cases of emergency. Employees shall be entitled to a thirty (30) minute unpaid meal break and fifteen (15) minute rest periods each day; one rest period to be taken during the shift worked prior to lunch, and one rest period to be taken during the shift worked after lunch. These rest periods are to be considered as worked time. If an employee is required to work more than ten (10) hours in any one workday, the employee shall be granted an additional fifteen minute rest period to be taken after the tenth (10th) hour worked.

During the term of this Agreement, the Employer will not simultaneously reduce the scheduled working hours of its regular full-time employees across the board and without regard to seniority. Whenever a reduction in the workforce is necessitated, the Employer will reduce the employee or employees affected, pursuant to Article 10 (Seniority). Schedules will be arranged to provide the maximum number of full-time employees with forty (40) hours per workweek schedules as is consistent with the requirements of the business with the understanding that hours will not be added unnecessarily to accomplish this objective.

B. All hours worked in excess of forty (40) hours in any workweek shall be overtime. Minimum rate of pay for the shift shall be time and one-half (1 1/2) the employee's basic rate of pay.

2

--- Page 3 ---

c. Any time worked in excess of eight (8) hours in any one (1) day shall be considered overtime and the minimum rate of pay shall be time and one-half (1 1/2) the regular base rate of pay.

D. All time worked in excess of forty (40) hours after the fifth (5th) full day worked during any workweek shall be overtime and the employee's minimum rate of pay shall be time and one-half (1 1/2) the regular base rate of pay.

E. All hours worked in excess of thirty-two (32) hours (two holidays fall within the same workweek) shall be considered overtime and shall be paid at the rate of time and one-half (1 1/2) the regular base rate of pay.

F. Hours of work at the above wage rate shall be between 6:30 a.m. and 6:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, and 7:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., for Saturday and days preceding shifts. Hours worked before 6:30 a.m. and after 6:30 p.m., except as above provided, shall be thirty-five cents (35¢) more per hour above the regular rate. Work performed on Sundays and holidays shall not be included in determining worked in the workweek.

G. Work performed on Sundays shall be paid at no less than time and one-half (1 1/2) the regular rate of pay.

H. Work performed on holidays shall be paid at no less than two (2) times an employee's regular rate of pay for all hours actually worked.

I. There shall be no split shift schedules for any employee.

J. In no case will overtime penalty or premium pay be pyramided.

K. 1. The hours for each employee shall be scheduled by the Employer. A work schedule for full-time employees for the succeeding work week, including Sunday or a holiday of the following week, shall be posted in the work area not later than 4:00 p.m. on the Friday of the current work week.

2. Schedules shall not be changed during the workweek, without the consent of the employees, unless necessary because of necessitated service breaks, fire, flood, etc.) Employees' schedules will not be changed to avoid payment of overtime, except on allowed days off.

3. An employee who is required to work on a scheduled day off shall receive time and one-half (1 1/2) for all day worked performed on that day. (The scheduled day off is the one posted on the Friday, or any delayed revisions performed to that day.)

L. A work schedule for part-time employees for the succeeding work week shall be posted in each market by 4:00 p.m. on the Friday of the current workweek, provided, however, the Employer may change the schedule of any part-time employee during any part of the workweek if business conditions necessitate such change.

M. Time spent by an employee traveling during the workday between two (2) stores of the Employer, at the request of the Employer, shall be considered time worked and the employees who are authorized to use their own transportation shall receive fifteen cents (15¢) per mile for the distance involved.

N. No employee shall be required to work more than five (5) hours without an unpaid lunch period.

O. Any full-time employee who reports for work as scheduled, without previous notice not to report, shall be guaranteed a minimum of his scheduled hours, whether he works one day, or four (4) hours of work or pay, whichever is greater, except in cases of emergencies as defined in Paragraph K-2.

P. If employees are required to attend store meetings, sales meetings or other Company-sponsored meetings outside of scheduled daily work or weekly work hours, such time shall be considered as time worked.

Q. Where work is performed, but not recorded, the employee involved will be entitled to payment including discharge. Employees who record another employee's time shall be disciplined, including discharge.

R. Employees shall be paid weekly.

S. Late shift or night shift work shall not be assigned for disciplinary reasons.

ARTICLE VII
VACATIONS

A. All full-time employees covered by this Contract, who have been employed full-time for the anniversary year, shall receive:

1) After one (1) year, one (1) week's vacation with pay;
2) After three (3) years, two (2) week's vacation with pay;
3) After seven (7) years, three (3) week's vacation with pay;
4) After fifteen (15) years, four (4) week's vacation with pay;
5) After twenty (20) years, five (5) week's vacation with pay.

Each week's vacation shall be no run less than six (6) consecutive working days.

B. A qualifying part-time employee, who has completed twelve (12) month's continuous service, will be eligible to receive a vacation with pay, provided that the part-time employee has worked six hundred twenty-four (624), or more, hours during the anniversary year.

Each part-time employee who meets the eligibility requirements of this Section of this Article, on his anniversary date, shall be entitled to receive: One (1) week's pro rata vacation with pay to be calculated on the basis of the total hours worked during the applicable anniversary year divided by fifty-two (52) weeks.

Part-time employees shall be entitled to a second (2nd) week of pro-rated vacation after completion of three (3) years service. Two weeks shall constitute the maximum allowable pro-rated vacation for part-time employees.

A full-time employee who is reduced to part-time because of reduction in work shall be entitled to a pro-rated vacation with pay, the vacation earned (if any) on a pro rata basis determined by dividing total hours worked in the vacation qualifying year by 52.

C. Vacation time to be consumed to start from employee of anniversary date or a date mutually agreed and agreed that vacation time shall be at a time convenient to both the employee and the Employer. It is agreed that the employee's vacation will be paid at his/her current weekly rate of pay. It is agreed that the Employer will consult with, and give due regard to the recommendations of, the Union representative when scheduling vacations, and in determining whether or not a replacement or replacements are necessary when vacations are being taken; provided, however, that after the Employer has fully considered the recommendations of the Head Meat Cutter and the Union representative, the Employer shall consult with the Head Meat Cutter and the Union representative regarding the matter, the Employer's decision on whether or not a replacement or replacements are necessary shall be concluded.

D.  The time for vacation eligibility: 1) A full-time employee will be eligible for a one-week vacation as of the first anniversary date of continuous full-time service, provided he has completed one (1) year of continuous full-time service as of that date.

2) After qualifying for his first one-week vacation, a full-time employee who has completed one (1) year of continuous full-time service (but less than three (3) years prior) to January 1 is eligible for a one-week vacation as of January 1.

3) A full-time employee will become eligible for a second week of vacation as of the third anniversary date of his beginning date of continuous full-time service provided he has completed three (3) years of continuous full-time service as of that date.

4) After qualifying for his first two-week vacation, a full-time employee who has completed three (3) years of continuous full-time service prior to January 1 is eligible for a two-week vacation as of January 1.

5) A full-time employee will become eligible for a third week of vacation as of the seventh anniversary date of his beginning date of continuous full-time service provided he has completed seven (7) years of continuous full-time service as of that date.

--- Page 4 ---

(6) Quarterly after his first three-week vacation, a full-time employee who has completed seven (7) years of continuous full-time service prior to January 1 is eligible for a three-week vacation as of January 1.

(7) A full-time employee will become eligible for a fourth week of vacation upon the fifteenth anniversary of his employment beginning date of continuous full-time service provided he has completed fifteen (15) years of continuous full-time service as of that date.

(8) Quarterly after his first four-week vacation, a full-time employee who has completed fifteen (15) years of continuous full-time service prior to January 1 is eligible for a four-week vacation as of January 1.

(9) A full-time employee will become eligible for a fifth week of vacation as of the twentieth anniversary of his employment beginning date of continuous full-time service provided he has completed twenty (20) years of continuous full-time service as of that date.

(10) Quarterly after his first five-week vacation, a full-time employee who has completed twenty (20) years of continuous full-time service prior to January 1 is eligible for a five-week vacation as of January 1.

If a full-time employee applies for a one (1), two (2), three (3), four (4) or five week vacation as of January 1 and is due to complete the service necessary for an additional week of vacation later in the year, he may take his earned vacation either way and take his cumulative earned vacation later in the year since he must have completed the service necessary for the additional week of vacation.

Effective November 16, 1980, part-time employees who have become full-time after that date, shall have all service full count of time from hire date when considered for calculations concerning vacation and eligibility.

F. If a full-time employee, who has not taken the vacation which he has earned by reason of his service is terminated for any reason except disciplinary reasons, he shall receive his vacation pay as equity at the time of termination.

F. When a holiday included in this Contract occurs during the calendar week of an employee's vacation, the employee, at his option, will be entitled to an extra day of vacation, or an extra day of pay in lieu thereof; however, if the employee requests the extra day he must provide his vacation pay informer of his request.

G. Choice of vacation dates will be granted on the basis of seniority in the market.

H. Employees shall be paid their vacation pay prior to their vacation period.

I. Employees entitled to vacations will not be given pay in lieu thereof, unless mutually agreed to by the Employer, the employee and the Union.

J. After one (1) year of employment, any leave of absence notting tenancy within (90) days or less any leave in any calendar year shall not affect vacation earned in that year; leaves totaling more than ninety (90) days but not over one hundred eighty eight (188) days shall reduce vacation and vacation pay by one-fourth (1/4); leaves totaling more than one hundred eighty eight (188) days but not over two hundred seventy (270) days shall reduce vacation and vacation pay by one-half (1/2); leaves totaling more than two hundred seventy (270) days shall disqualify the employee for vacation for that year only.

K. Should ownership change during the term of this Contract, the present Employer agrees to pay employees for that portion of vacation earned up to date change is made.

ARTICLE III
HOLIDAYS

A. A full holiday shall be given to all full-time non-probability employees covered by this Contract on the following days without reduction in pay:

(1) New Year's Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day and the employee's anniversary date.

(2) After the completion of one (1) year (only) in employment with Employer, employees shall be entitled to the following additional holidays in accordance with this Contract:

Three (3) personal holidays shall be taken at a time mutually agreed upon between the Employer and the employee. The employee's birthday itself shall also be celebrated as a personal holiday.

Holidays falling on Sunday shall be celebrated the following Monday. When an employee's birthday or anniversary date falls during a holiday week when the employee is not scheduled off day and pay with him will be given the next succeeding non-holiday week end.

B. The following holidays shall be considered as paid holidays for all qualifying part-time employees.

(1) New Year's Day
(2) Fourth of July
(3) Labor Day
(4) Thanksgiving Day
(5) Christmas Day
(6) Employee's Birthday
(7) Employee's Anniversary Date
(8) Employee's Personal Day
(9) Employee's Personal Day
(10) Employee's Personal Day

The following shall govern how holiday pay allowance for the above enumerated holidays be recovered not:

Any employee who shall have received compensation for an average of over twelve (12) hours during the four (4) calendar weeks immediately preceding any such working week in which the holiday falls and, who works during the working week during which the holiday occurs shall receive a holiday pay allowance equal to the average daily hours he has worked during such preceding four (4) calendar weeks, divided by five (5).

When a part-time employee, who is otherwise eligible for holiday pay allowance under the conditions prescribed above is scheduled to work for an employee who has rescheduled a holiday and falls to work, or to work the scheduled day before or day after the holiday, the employee shall receive holiday pay for the day he works.

C. An employee will not receive holiday or birthday pay if he is absent without excuse his scheduled shift hour after the holiday or birthday or his birthday if he is absent without excuse his scheduled shift hour after the holiday or on his birthday or his birthday, if so scheduled. An employee will not lose his holiday or birthday pay if his absence is caused by proven illness, or if his absence has been mutually agreed to, provided he has worked any part of the holiday or birthday. To work on his birthday or holiday or birthday week. The Union agrees that any employee, in order to be eligible for birthday pay, shall give written notice to the Head Meat Cutter during her second week prior to the date of his birthday.

ARTICLE IX
LEAVES OF ABSENCE

A. In case of death of a member of the immediate family of any regular full-time employee, such employee shall be entitled to an excused absence for such time as the Employer deems reasonably necessary in connection with the occurrence. And thereby the first three (3) days' excused absence from his regularity shift shall be with full pay and thereafter any excused absence shall be without hours pay and shall not be considered as hours worked for overtime purposes. No extra pay allowance shall be paid for deaths multiple or simultaneous deaths occurring within any three-service period. No day allowance shall be granted in any case whatever, because of distance, or other cause, the employee foot the expense.

By immediate family is meant to include spouse, son, daughter, mother, father, sister, brother, mother-in-law, father-in-law, grandmother, grandfather-and grandchildren.

B. The Employer agrees to grant the necessary time off without discrimination a reasonable rights and without pay to not more than two (2) employees out one (1) store, and no more than five (5) employees from the Employer, designated by the Union to attend Union business, provided the Employer is given at least one (1) week's notice, in writing, from the Union, specifying the length of time off, and in no case shall the length of time off exceed one (1) year.

--- Page 5 ---

“An employee who has been promoted or assigned to an exempt management position may be reassigned to the bargaining unit by the Employer and if reassigned to the bargaining unit within six (6) months, shall retain his/her seniority.

C. Service for the purpose of determining wage increases under the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall be credited for time spent on approved leave of absence, provided that such absence is not in excess of thirty (30) days. However, on the employee’s return to work from such leave of absence, service for the purpose of determining wage increases under the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall begin again.

D. An employee desiring a leave of absence must secure written permission from the Employer, except as otherwise provided within this Contract. The length of absence shall be agreed upon by the Employees and the Employer. Failure to report back to work at the absence shall be deemed a voluntary quit. Any employee accepting employment elsewhere while on leave of absence shall be considered a voluntary quit, except in a case where such employment works for the Union. Under Section D, an employee who is granted a leave of absence for more than thirty (30) days increases the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall be restricted until the period for time the user time of absence begins but absence is not accrued during such leave of absence which is in excess of thirty (30) days. However, on the employee’s return to work from such leave of absence, service for the purpose of determining wage increases under the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall begin accrue.

E. Any employee in Military Service under the provisions of the Federal law shall be entitled to return to his/her job in accordance with those laws and retain his seniority in accordance with those laws.

F. When an employee is required for service on the jury, he shall receive the difference between his regular straight-time rate and the amount received for jury duty provided the employee notified the Employer within twenty-four (24) hours after receiving the jury summons. An employee who is called away from jury service provided that any on scheduled workday, the employee shall promptly report to complete any remaining hours of his scheduled workday.

G. Leaves of absence because of sickness, pregnancy, or injury not to exceed an extended period of time shall be granted to any employee who has been employed at least thirty-one (31) days upon written request to the Employer supported by medical evidence. Extensions will be given up to ninety (90) days at a time for a cumulative total of one (1) year, or (in case an employee has had a previous leave of absence for sickness, pregnancy, or injury within the last twelve (12) consecutive months of full employment) ninety (90) service, and granted in writing, supported by proper medical evidence provided prior to each expiration.

In exceptional cases, additional leaves may be considered by the Employer based upon the employee’s record, disciplinary history, the Employer’s service, and probability of being able to again perform the job. Service for the purpose of determining wage increases under the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall be retained for the period prior to the time such leave of absence begins, but absence is not accrued during such leave of absence which is in excess of thirty (30) days. However, on the date the employee returns to work from such leave of absence, service, for the purpose of determining wage increases under the wage progression scale set forth in Appendix A shall begin accrue.

ARTICLE X
SENIORITY

A. Seniority for full-time employees shall be followed by the Employer, in each seniority area separately, such seniority areas or zones to be mutually agreed upon between the Employer and the Union, for the following classifications:

1. Head Meat Cutters
2. Journeyman Meat Cutters
3. Apprentice Meat Cutters
4. Weighers & Wrappers
5. Seafood Clerks

* (Effective December 1, 1983, Apprentice Meat Cutters and Journeyman Meat Cutters classifications shall be combined on the same seniority list.)

In cases of layoffs and recalls after layoffs, if skills are comparable and the seniority list is combined, the Employer will perform the work. Seniority areas are described in Appendix “B” “ attached to this Agreement.

B. In the event of a reduction in hours and/or layoff of full-time employees in a market, the least senior employee in the job classification in the market affected by such reduction or layoff may replace the least senior full-time employee in the seniority area in the job classification.

C. In the event of a recalls by employer after layoff or reduction of hours, such employees on layoff or reduced hours status shall be called back to work and/or have their hours restored in the order of their seniority in the job classification in the seniority area.

D. Seniority for part-time employees shall be followed by the Employer in each store separately only for the purposes of layoffs and recalls, for the following classifications:

1. Journeyman Meat Cutters
2. Apprentice Meat Cutters
3. Weighers and Wrappers
4. Seafood Clerks

* (Effective December 1, 1983, Apprentice Meat Cutters and Journeyman Meat Cutters classifications shall be combined on the same seniority list.)

E. The Employer shall post semi-annually separate seniority lists by job classification for all full-time employees in each seniority area in each store and for all part-time employees who have been employed at least ninety (90) working days:

F. The Employer shall furnish to the Union a duplicate copy of each of seniority lists for all full-time and all part-time employees.

G. The original posted seniority lists shall establish the seniority of each employee who does not, in writing, protest his seniority within thirty (30) days after such seniority has had the opportunity to observe such seniority list.

H. Seniority for full-time and part-time employees shall be based upon the length of continuous service with the Employer in the particular job classification in the seniority area, except as otherwise provided herein.

I. Seniority for full-time and part-time employees begins to accrue after an employee completes thirty (30) days of employment in the job classification with which he is assigned. If the employee is a transfer, the date of seniority is the date the employee is employed on the thirtieth day shall date from the date of such employment in the job classification with the Employer, if the employee is reassigned in the service of the Employer between two probationary period.

J. When an employee is promoted to a higher classification or changes his Journeyman classification, his seniority as a full-time Journeyman shall determine the date beginning of his full-time employment with the Employer.

K. The Employer shall have the right to release any employee for any cause whatsoever without recourse, provided such employee is released within thirty- (30) days from the date of the employee’s employment.

L. An employee’s seniority shall terminate upon the occurrence of any of the following events:

(1) Employee quits.
(2) Employee is discharged for just cause.
(3) Employee fails to return to work within seventy-two (72) hours after being called back to employment by registered mail or telegram at his last known address.
(4) Employee has not been on the active payroll of the Employer for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months.

M. Employer agrees to advise the Union promptly of all layoffs, discharges, recalls and personnel transfers of full-time employees.

N. Any regular full-time employee who would be laid off for lack of work will first be offered the maximum number of part-time hours available in his classification in the seniority area. If he accepts the offer to work part-time in lieu of layoff, he will be placed at the top of the part-time seniority list.

--- Page 6 ---

N. A full-time employee who is reduced to part-time because of a reduction in hours by the Employer works hours by the Employer shall retain his full-time seniority for (2) two years after being reduced to part-time.

Q. A full-time employee who is reduced to part-time with the approval of the Employer at the employee's written request shall lose their full-time seniority; however they shall have preference over a new employee for a full-time job their preference in their store only.

P. When a Journeyman is promoted to Head Meat Cutter, he shall retain seniority in the Journeyman's classification.

Q. In the event of store closing, the Head Meat Cutter in each store shall retain seniority in the Journeyman classification. Service in the Head Meat Cutter classification immediately prior to his most recent appointment as a Head Meat Cutter shall be credited to his Journeyman classification seniority. In case a Head Meat Cutter is transferred to another store or is promoted to a higher classification or is transferred to another store as Head Meat Cutter, the displaced Head Meat Cutter shall retain seniority as a Journeyman, including his service in his most recent appointment as a Head Meat Cutter.

R. In the event the Employer closes or sells a store, the employees two (2) or more with the most seniority may displace the least senior employee in their classification (Head Meat Cutter considered Junior most Journeyman Meat Cutter) within the jurisdiction of Local No. 400. No employees thus displaced shall have any recourse against the Employer or the Union.

S. When two or more full-time employees are hired into the same job classification on the same date in the same seniority area, the Employer shall, at such time as it becomes date material, advertise the Union of their seniority status.

T. Transfers of full-time employees are permitted between markets of the Employer in the seniority area or zone, provided seniority is transferred. Transfers shall be based on legitimate business needs. Seniority for all transfers shall be based on seniority in the area and zone, except for vacation relief, or illness, or store closure. Unless otherwise agreed to in writing in special cases by the Employer and the Union. Employees transferred for vacation relief or to act as me relief because of illness shall be returned to the store from which he was transferred immediately upon the return of the employee on vacation relief or because of illness, seniority in the market will be followed.

U. When a full-time employee is transferred into another seniority area at his request, such employee shall be placed at the bottom of the seniority list if he is a new employee in that classification, or shall lose his seniority if he is transferred. When a full-time employee is transferred into another seniority area at the Employer's request, such employee's seniority in the seniority area into which such employee has been transferred shall include his seniority prior to the transfer.

V. A Head Meat Cutter who is demoted to Journeyman for any reason whatsoever, shall have his continuous service credits transferred to the Journeyman seniority group.

W. Part-time employees shall be given the first opportunity for permanent full-time jobs in their classification based on seniority in their respective stores before new employees are hired for such full-time jobs.

Where no part-time employee within a store desires full-time work, employees working less than forty (40) hours in the area and who have previously indicated in writing to the Employer their desire for full-time work, shall be given the first opportunity for full-time work based upon seniority within the area.

The Employer will schedule all work for part-time employees based on seniority within their classification within their store not to exceed eight (8) hours in any one (1) day or forty (40) hours in any one (1) week, provided the employee is qualified and available for at least four (4) consecutive hours when the work is available and that this scheduling does not conflict with or prohibit the scheduling of a full-time employee in that classification in that store. However, this scheduling is not intended to mean that the Employer must schedule so as to incur additional premiums or penalties or violate any provisions of the Agreement. The part-time employee who desires full-time work shall notify the Store Manager that he is available for a posted schedule within twenty-four (24) hours after the posted schedule is set and provide he has no claim on his schedule of hours cutting.

Part-time employees by classification with the most seniority within a store will be given the part-time schedule with the most hours, provided they are qualified to perform the work required and are immediately available.

X. During the term of this Agreement, the Employer will not reduce the scheduled hours of its regular full-time employees on the payroll as of November 15, 1975, unless a layoff occurs or a reduction has occurred in accordance with the parties' side letter regarding the proper interpretation of Section N of Article 10 Seniority), until the following:

(1) All part-time employees by classification who were on the payroll April 15, 1975, and not covered by Health and Welfare and Pension are laid off in that store.

(2) All part-time employees by classification who are covered by Health and Welfare and Pension (twenty-four (24) hours or more) on the effective date of this Agreement are reduced by seniority to a schedule of two-twenty four (24) hours or more.

(3) All part-time employees by classification as outlined in (2) above are reduced to lavous status in that store.

(4) Notwithstanding the provisions above, the Employer will assign work on seniority basis to a full-time employee in more than one store in an area to maintain his or her forty (40) hour schedule. If said employee refuses said assignment, he or she forfeits their claim to the scheduled hours.

Y. Definition of a full-time employee: All employees on the full-time seniority list as of April 15, 1975, and not covered by Health and Welfare who darts forty (40) hours per week for six (6) weeks during an eight-week period shall be considered as working full-time (40 hours) due to the absence of another full-time employee.

When an employee qualifies as outlined above, their full-time seniority date shall be the date of the beginning of the qualification period.

Z. When a full-time employee in the Journeyman or Weighers and Wrappers classifications desires to move to another store in his or her seniority area, the employee will give notification, in writing, to an official designated by the Store Manager, the Personnel Manager and the Union, stating the store or stores he desires to move. When there is a bona fide vacancy in his or her classification in such store, the employee's request for transfer will be considered based on seniority and ability to perform the work.

Z-1. Department seniority for a separate classification with separate seniority. In the event of a layoff, Meat Cutters (Journeymen) on payroll as of ratification) may apply their seniority into the Seafood Department in lieu of being laid off, at their current rate of pay, on the therefore Seafood Department Clerk rate whichever is less. Present Seafood Department employees, upon notice of layoff, may apply their seniority in order to bump into the Meat Department. If they decide to stay in the Seafood Department they will remain in the Seafood Department only then apply to the Seafood Department only in the event of layoff or of layoffs (this applies only to those Seafood Department employees who were on the payroll as of ratification) may exercise their seniority into the Meat Department.

Seafood Clerks hired after ratification of this agreement shall have seniority in the Seafood Department only. Should a Seafood Clerk desire promotion to a higher classification, such Clerk shall make their wishes known to their Zone Manager in writing with copies to the Personnel Manager and the Union. Such Seafood Clerk will be considered by seniority from those who have made their wishes known in writing.

6

--- Page 7 ---

ARTICLE XI
WORKING CONDITIONS

A. Union Shop Cards may be displayed in markers which employ members of the Union. The Local Union Secretary-Treasurer or his authorized agent has the full power to remove said card upon violation of any part of this Contract. Cards will be displayed in a conspicuous place.

B. Business Agents of the Union shall be admitted at all reasonable times to the working room or rooms and interview the employees covered by this Agreement.

C. As the employees engaged under this Agreement can be members of the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union, nothing in this Contract shall be construed as to interfere with any lawful obligation which they may be subject to as members of Food and Commercial Workers International Union as members thereof.

D. The Union agrees to cooperate in correcting inefficient employments of employees which might otherwise necessitate discharge.

E. The employer agrees not to enter into any agreement or understanding with any employee covered by this Contract, individually or collectively, which would limit the benefits of this Agreement.

F. The Employer shall furnish all necessary tools of the trade, laundry, hairnet and/or uniforms when required, provide the Employer, whenever applicable, shall furnish to the female employees adornment uniforms or similar type uniforms. The employees who are furnished such uniforms shall be responsible in the event for the loss of these uniforms and such uniforms shall be laundered by the employees.

G. The Employer will provide bulletin boards or equivalent notice place in a section suitable selected by the Union. The Employer may post notices necessary for conducting Union business on such boards or other suitable space.

H. Contributions to charitable causes shall not be compulsory.

I. The Employer agrees to furnish and maintain a first aid kit in a designated place and to check said kit monthly to replenish any designated supplied pieces.

J. Employee agree to provide guards on grinders and cube machines. No employee shall use a grinder without the guard on the mill or use the cube machine with the lid or guard up. Any employee using the above equipment without the safety guards shall be subject to discipline, including discharge, without recourse to the arbitration.

K. No employee will be required to report for work until said employee has had a minimum of (10) ten hours off duty.

L. Employees shall not be required to take a polygraph test.

ARTICLE XII
GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION

A. The Employer recognizes the right of the Union to designate one (1) Shop Steward in each market. Such steward shall be designated in writing to the Employer by the Union.

B. Should any differences, disputes, or complaints arise over the interpretation or application of the contents of this Contract, there shall be an efficient sort of the amounts of the party both seres to promptly settle through the following procedure:

Step 1. By conference between the aggrieved employee, the Shop Steward, or Business Agent, and the Manager, and the store of the Manager.

Step 2. By a conference between the Shop Steward or the Business Agent of the Union and the Zone Manager, District Manager or District Supervisor of the Employer, if such exists, within five (5) working days after the completion of Step 1.

Step 3. By a conference between an official of the Union and a designated official of the Employer, within five (5) working days after the completion of Step 2.

Step 4. In the event the grievance is not settled through the abovementioned steps, it shall be referred to arbitration.

C. Grievances must be reduced to writing by the aggrieved employee after the completion of Step 2 in order to be considered under Step 3 and prior to be submitted in writing to official in lieu of notices.

D. Grievances presented later than seven (7) calendar days after the occurrence of the event complained of will not be considered.

E. The grievance that issues may arise of a general nature affecting nature or extending to more than one (1) employee covered by this Contract and that issues need not be subject to the entire grievance procedure, but may be initiated at any of the above-mentioned steps deemed appropriate by the Union representative handling the grievance.

F. It is understood that the Union Grievance Committee shall make the final decision as to arriving at a settlement or any grievance initiated by an employee covered by this Contract. No grievance shall be submitted to arbitration without the approval of the Union representative of the Union Grievance Committee.

G. It is understood and agreed and all employees covered by this Contract must exercise all their rights, privileges, and necessary procedures under this Contract in the settlement of any complaint or grievance.

H. One (1) person shall be appointed by the Employer and one (1) person shall be appointed by the Union (if two (2) persons are unable to settle the complaint, either the Employer or the Union may, within the two (2) days since the complaint, disagree the Request of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service to appoint an impartial arbitrator. The third person shall be the Arbitrator shall be chosen. The decision of the Arbitrator shall be binding on all parties. The Union shall strike a name from the pen, then the Employer shall strike a name, in this order, until one (1) person's name remains, who shall be the Arbitrator. The expenses of the representative of the Arbitrator shall be paid for equally by the Employer and the Union.

I. The Employer may, at any time, at discharge, any worker for just cause. The Union, if it wishes to contest the discharge, may file a written complaint with the Employer within five (5) working days. Such complaint must be taken up promptly and shall be settled within five (5) working days or within forty-eight (48) hours, it shall be referred, within twenty-four (24) hours, to arbitration.

J. No Arbitrator shall have the authority to alter, amend or change any term or provisions of this Contract.

ARTICLE XIII
SEPARATION PAY

A full-time employee will receive no more than six (6) months' full-time service, who is permanently reduced separation the functions of the job, store closing or reduction in the working forces, shall be given one (1) week's notice or one (1) week's pay in lieu of notice. An employee separated during a week for any of these reasons is entitled to pay their pension up to the day of his dismissal, plus one day for an additional week notice, which, at the option of the Employer, may be paid in week or in lieu of notice.

ARTICLE XIV
HEALTH AND WELFARE

A. The Employer shall contribute to the established Health and Welfare Trust Fund the sum of one hundred ninety-one dollars and eleven cents quarterly ($191.11) per month for each employee who has completed an average of twenty-four (24) hours per week for a period of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours) and shall continue to contribute one hundred ninety-one dollars and eleven cents quarterly ($191.11) per month for each employee who maintains an average of twenty-four (24) hours per week for a period of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours). Employees who are off work and receiving Employer sickness pay and/or accident benefits shall have such time counted as hours worked immediately preceding the first day of the calendar month.

Effective with employees hired after November 13, 1983, the following additional eligibility rules shall apply:

--- Page 8 ---

(1) The Employer contribution shall commence on the 1st of the month following six (6) full months of employment.

(2) Any employee hired by the Employer who was covered by the District Trust Fund as of the date this hire shall have a contribution made on their behalf by the first of the month following the date of hire.

(3) Before the four (4) consecutive calendar weeks referred to in Section A above first occur, the Employer shall make a contribution for the month immediately preceding the first day of the calendar month, which period shall be the period used for determination of continuation of the contribution on consecutive calendar weeks or employment.

C. Effective November 1, 1984, and November 1, 1985, Health and Welfare contributions shall be increased in the amount necessary (if any) to maintain those benefits in effect as of October 23, 1985, now in effect since the last increase.

Such maintenance of benefit increases to be capped to the extent that funds held in reserve by the Trust Fund, in excess of four (4) months reserves, will be first used to offset the required increase in contributions for maintenance of benefits on November 1, 1984, and November 1, 1985.

D. Contributions to the Trust Fund shall be discontinued as of the first of the month following:

1. A layoff or leave of absence of thirty (30) calendar days or more, except as otherwise provided below;

2. The employee's ceasing to be an eligible employee due to his failure to work an average of twenty-four (24) hours or more per week for four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours).

E. Contributions to the Trust Fund shall be continued under the following conditions:

1. In case of a non-work accident, one (1) month's contribution following the month in which the employee incurred the accident.

2. In case of pregnancy, two (2) months' contribution after the month in which the employee begins her pregnancy leave of absence.

3. In case of illness, two (2) months' contribution following the month in which the illness occurs.

4. In case of compensable injury, three (3) months' contribution following the month in which the injury occurs.

5. The Employer agrees to pay the contributions to the Trust Fund for eligible employees for one (1) month following termination of employment, except for those employees who are discharged for cause.

F. An actuarial study will be made to determine the extent of providing the contributions to the Trust Fund for eligible employees through the Health and Welfare Trust Fund and the Employer may, at his option elect to provide the coverage required under this Section through the Health and Welfare Trust.

G. If the Employer fails to make any contribution as required by the Trustees an employer penalty per incidence shall be assessed.

It is further agreed that if the Administrator becomes necessary to sue the Employer to collect any contribution due hereunder, the Employer shall also be responsible for paying all of the necessary court costs and reasonable attorneys' fees incurred in connection with the collection of such contributions as well, as said ten percent (10%) penalty.

ARTICLE XV
PENSIONS

A. The Employer agrees to contribute in part and contribute to the United Fund and Commercial Workers International Union Industry Pension Trust Fund, which Fund and has shall maintain Treasury Department Approval. Employer will not be obligated to make any contributions to the Fund until the Fund is approved by the Treasury Department.

B. The Employer agrees to contribute to the jointly administered National Pension Trust Fund the sum of one hundred twenty-nine dollars and thirty-one cents ($129.31) per salaried month per eligible employee covered by this Contract.

Effective July 1, 1984 — $ 125.60
July 1, 1985 — $ 134.20
July 1, 1986 — $ 142.80

C. The term "eligible employee" shall mean an employee who has worked an average of twenty-four (24) hours per week for a period of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours). Such an employee becomes eligible for participation in the pension program on the first day of the calendar month immediately following the pension program on the first day of the calendar month immediately following the first occurrence of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours) and such date hereafter referred to as his eligibility date.

D. Contributions to the Pension Fund shall be discontinued as of the first of the month immediately following:

1. A layoff or leave of absence of thirty (30) calendar days or more, except as otherwise provided below;

2. The employee's ceasing to be an eligible employee due to his failure to work an average of twenty-four (24) hours or more per week for four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours).

E. Contributions to the Pension Fund, discontinued as set forth in Section D above, shall be resumed as of the first of the month following return from layoff or leave of absence.

F. Contributions to the Pension Fund shall be continued under the following conditions:

1. In case of a non-work accident, one (1) month's contribution following the month in which the employee incurred the accident.

2. In case of pregnancy, two (2) months' contribution after the month in which the employee begins her pregnancy leave of absence.

3. In case of illness, two (2) months' contribution following the month in which the illness occurs.

4. In case of compensable injury, three (3) months' contribution following the month in which the injury occurs.

5. The Employer agrees to pay the contributions to the Pension Fund for eligible employees for one (1) month following termination of employment.

G. When the Employer commences payments into this Pension Fund, the employees covered by this Contract shall automatically cease to participate in the Employer's previous pension plan.

H. The parties to the bargaining agreement for each of the affected employees of the Employer, agrees on behalf of each of the said employees who are not participants in said existing Employer's Retirement Plan, unilaterally established by the Employer, that each of said employees, in consideration of the benefits to be derived from the Pension Fund, hereby agrees to waive, enabling his or her employees to make participation therein, shall withdraw from and surrender, release and relinquish whatever rights, privileges and benefits he, her any, in the Employer's Retirement Plan, effective with the date the Employer commences payment.

ARTICLE XVI
MANAGEMENT RIGHTS

A. The management of the store(s) and direction of the working forces, including the right to plan, direct, expand, reduce and control operations, hire, assign, suspend or discharge for proper cause, to relieve employees from duty because of lack of work or for other proper reasons, the right to introduce any new machinery, equipment or methods of operation, and to make such regulations as may be necessary or desirable for the operation of a store shall be vested exclusively in the Employer.

B. It is expressly understood and agreed that all rights which the Employer had prior to the execution of this Agreement, except where explicitly limited by the terms of this Agreement, are preserved and shall continue to be vested in the Employer. In the event any rules or regulations and regulations are promulgated, the Employer agrees that it will furnish copies of such rules and regulations to the Union, and with other post them on the bulletin boards or supply each employee with a copy.

8

--- Page 9 ---

ARTICLE XVII
FAVORED NATIONS CLAUSE

Should the Union at any time hereafter enter into an agreement with any major employer (Safeway, Lucky Stores D/B/A Eagle Bounty) the same agreement be used as the Employer business signatory hereunto written within Harris County surveyed the best Employer with the terms and conditions more advantageous to such other employee than is provided for in this Agreement, then the Employer, party to this Agreement, shall be provided with similar or such advantageous terms and conditions.

ARTICLE XVIII
SAVINGS CLAUSE

Should any part or provision of any provision herein contained be rendered or deemed or declared invalid by reason of any existing or subsequently enacted legislation or by decree of a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidation of such part or portion of this Agreement shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions hereof and they shall remain in full force and effect thereinafter.

ARTICLE XIX
STORE CLOSING

A. In the event the Employer closes a store and some employees are terminated as a result sevenday notice and severance pay and severance pay true to one % (one%) week's pay for each year of continuous service, commencing with the (3rd) year of continuous service for employees up to 10yr, but not to exceed eight (8) weeks' pay at their regular rate. However, those employees who semoga’s [sic] have been employed less than three years as an employee will receive pro rata severance pay for that years as follows:
* 0-3 months equals twenty five percent (25%) of a week's pay
* 3-6 months equals thirty five percent (50%) of a week's pay
* 6-9 months equals seventy five percent (75%) of a week's pay
* Over 9 months equals one (1) week's pay
Severance pay shall be computed on the average hours worked per week for the fifty-two (52) weeks preceding a voluntary layoff or termination.

B. Employees terminated as a result of store closing shall receive in addition to severance pay pro rata vacation pay.
The Employer shall continue contributions to the Pension and Health and Welfare Trust Fund for three (3) full months following termination for store employees who receive severance pay, except those employees who secure employment with a competing Employer including severance pay in the Pension and Health Welfare Trust fund.

D. All monies due employees including severance pay shall be paid in a lump sum payment.
E. The Employer agrees to give the employees and the Union four (4) weeks' notice of advance in the event of a store closing or sale. When such notice is given, an employee shall remain with the Employer until the store closes or forfeits the rights under this Article unless mutually agreed to by the employee, Employer and Union.

F. No benefits shall accrue under the terms of this Article, unless the Employer makes a business decision to close or sell a store. If a store is abolished by case incendio, fire storm, land condemnation, or remodeling, then this Article shall not apply.

G. No benefits shall accrue under the terms of this Article if the employee resigns before arriving within a seventy-five (75) mile radius.
Any employee who is terminated and who is eligible for and accepts, severance pay, forfeits all seniority and recall rights. An employee who does not accept severance pay shall retain his recall rights for a period of six (6) months, and if still not recalled by the Employer, then she shall receive his severance pay and has no further recall rights.

ARTICLE XX
INDIVIDUAL RETIREMENT ACCOUNT (IRA)

The Employer agrees to deduct from the wages of its employees those amounts designated by them and to remit of such amounts deducted to a single individual retirement account such account to be established. This deduction and establishment of this account not to be co cost to the Employer other than the normal cost of payroll deduction.

ARTICLE XXI
DURATION

A. This Contract shall become effective as of November 20, 1983, and shall continue in full force and effect through November 22, 1986, and shall be automatically renewed and extended from year to year thereafter, unless either party serves notice in writing on the other party at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration date or anniversary date thereforeafter, of a desire to terminate or change this Contract.

B. This Contract, when executed, shall be defined to mean the wages, hours and rates of pay and other conditions of employment of the employees covered by this Contract for the term of the Contract, and no new or additional agreements shall be valid unless approved hereby to be subject to the negotiation during the termination her term.

C. All of the agreed upon changes and revisions in the Agreement will be effective as of the first (1st) Monday following the ratification of the new Agreement unless otherwise specifically provided for by the Agreement in effect.

This Letter of Agreement shall be attached to and become a part of the Agreement between United Food and Commercial Workers, Local Union No. 408 and The Kroger Co., Houston, Texas, effective November 20, 1983, through November 20, 1985.

CLASSIFICATION OF ARTICLE X, SECTION N

It is agreed between the parties that when a full-time employee's hours are reduced to less than forty (40) but not less than thirty-two (32) hours per week, the employee will have the option of exercising their seniority to the least senior full-time position by classification in the zone (district) or the employee may remain at the store for an indefinite time working the reduced schedule.

If the employee elects to remain at the store working at least thirty-two (32) but less than forty (40) hours per week and at a later time decides to exercise their seniority, the employee must notify their store manager in writing by Wednesday noon for the following week's schedule.

If the full-time employee's hours are reduced to less than thirty-two (32) hours per week must exercise their seniority to "bump" the least senior full-time employee in their seniority classification in their seniority area or forfeit their full-time seniority and take the part-time job in the store. Such refusal shall be in writing.

It is understood that a full-time employee's option to remain at their store working less than forty (40) hours but not less than thirty-two (32) hours per week will waive that employee's right to file a time claim.

ARTICLE XVII
FAVORED NATIONS

Article XVII, Favored Nations Clause of the Agreement will not apply to newly organized companies during the term of their first (1st) collective bargaining agreement (not to exceed a maximum of three (3) years), or companies that are in bankrupt status so long as such company remains in bankrupt status.

ARTICLE VII
VACATIONS

A full-time employee who is reduced to part-time because of reduction in work hours by the Employer shall retain multiple weeks of vacation earned (if any) on a pro-rata basis determined by dividing total hours worked in the vacation qualifying year by 52.

Effective November 16, 1980, part-time employees who become full-time after that date, shall have all service from date of hire considered when calculating vacation eligibility.

If you concur in the above, please indicate by signing in the space provided below.
